text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — sustained high QPS for org 'FluxGate' (org_id=fg-823). Token queue growth detected on eu-west-1 cluster-12, tail latency spiking, 5xx rate ~6.3% over 5m, 429s ~2.0%. Auto-scaling attempted but custom per-org policy blocked burst overrides. Potential customer-impacting errors. Paging oncall.

devon (oncall): acked. looking. can someone confirm whether they're hitting a sudden new workload or if it's a retry storm?

maria (sre): joining — I'm seeing large contiguous KV cache misses from that org, lots of long-running requests. Logs show many identical prompt prefixes (~10k reqs / min) -> likely a bot or a bad rollout.

cheng (infra): yes from infra side: their requests are mostly short completions but very high QPS. autoscaler kept up but we hit per-org token rate ceiling. The organization has a strict quota that blocked our normal burst policy.

devon (oncall): customer-impact? any 500s returned to their users?

maria (sre): some 503/504 traces on the downstream pool when queue backs up — user-facing errors reported. Support ticket #CS-5241 started.

samir (prod): @jen please confirm with CS. We might need an emergency temporary rate tweak and to disable the noisy feature in their app if possible.

jen (customer-success): pinged customer (FluxGate eng lead) via email and slack. They confirm they rolled an A/B experiment an hour ago. They're already seeing degraded UX. Asked them to pause the rollout — waiting for reply.

alex (ops): recommendation: soft-throttle rather than full unthrottle. If we raise org limit too much it could blast shared pools. Propose apply an emergency soft-window: set per-org rate_limit_override to 60 rps with burst 300 for 30 minutes, enable queuing policy 'graceful-reject' so we return 429 early instead of 5xx.

devon (oncall): +1. That matches SLOs and keeps other tenants safe. Who can apply the override?

cheng (infra): I can. Using internal admin tool. Running command now (will run in canary first on eu-west-1 cluster-12):

```
# dry-run
redwood-admin orgs set-rate-override --org fg-823 --region eu-west-1 --rate 60 --burst 300 --duration 30m --mode canary
```

Then promote if canary looks stable:

```
redwood-admin orgs set-rate-override --org fg-823 --region all --rate 60 --burst 300 --duration 30m --mode promote
```

maria (sre): I'm watching the telemetry. Can we also flip kv-prefix caching to on for that org? It will reduce compute per request.

cheng (infra): can do, small config change:

```
redwood-admin orgs set-config --org fg-823 --kv_cache_prefetch=true
```

I'll apply after canary stabilizes.

support-bot: CS ticket #CS-5241 updated: emergency rate override requested; contacted on-call.

(devon performs quick checklist)
devon (oncall): rolling canary now. cheng?

cheng (infra): canary applied to cluster-12 at 16:05 UTC. Observing metrics...

maria (sre): within 2 minutes latency p95 dropped from 1.8s -> 0.9s for that org. 5xxs down by ~70%. No surprising side-effects yet.

jen (customer-success): FluxGate responded — they paused the A/B rollout. Appreciate the quick action. They asked whether we can leave the override for 1 hour and then re-evaluate.

alex (ops): I prefer 30m initial window with auto-extension option. Let's keep manual check at 30m mark. I'll create a rollback guard.

cheng (infra): promoting to global now. Running promote command.

```
redwood-admin orgs set-rate-override --org fg-823 --region all --rate 60 --burst 300 --duration 30m --mode promote
```

maria (sre): also enabled kv_cache_prefetch for fg-823. Watching memory usage — small bump but within budget.

support-bot: CS-5241: FluxGate confirmed temporary throttle accepted.

devon (oncall): good. I'm leaving an inherit note: applied soft override, kv prefetch on, auto-scaling unchanged. Followups: postmortem, detect-and-block pattern, consider automatic per-org burst exception gating.

samir (prod): action items -> 1) reach out to FluxGate PM for RCA and ask for their rollout guardrails; 2) add a telemetry alert for identical-prefix spike pattern; 3) evaluate option to auto-suspend feature flags that generate high identical traffic.

jen (customer-success): customer is satisfied for now. They asked for a short summary to share with their execs. I'll draft and send.

alex (ops): reminder: no full unthrottle. keep limits bounded. If we see cross-tenant impact we rollback immediately.

maria (sre): 30m check-in scheduled in thread. If stable, we close and create incident ticket for postmortem.

(30 minutes later)

maria (sre): 30m status: metrics stable, 5xxs back to baseline, p95 normalized. No collateral. I'll start incident timeline and assign postmortem to devon/samir.

devon (oncall): closing mitigation. Will keep the override active for another 15m then let it expire (no auto-extend). Please escalate if anything pops.

cheng (infra): override set to expire at 17:00 UTC (15m left).

jen (customer-success): FluxGate confirmed their users recovered. They're ok with closing.

support-bot: CS-5241 marked resolved (pending postmortem).

devon (oncall): postmortem owners: devon (oncall), samir (prod). I'll include timeline, root cause (customer rollout + missing guard), mitigations performed, and follow-ups (detect identical-prefix spikes, safer default burst policy, per-org automated burst gating).

samir (prod): also adding action: update docs for on-call runbook for per-org emergency overrides and include the exact redwood-admin commands.

maria (sre): closing thread. Great cross-team work. :tada:
